Class TrafficLineGraphBuilder

java.lang.Object
preprocessing.TrafficLineGraphBuilder
public class TrafficLineGraphBuilder extends Object
Preprocessor for network traffic data, as proposed by R. W. R. Darling, and implemented by Dukotah Hutcheon (2026).

Input is a CSV file where each line is: record ID, source address, destination address, time stamp. The time stamp must be numerical (for example, seconds since the epoch). A header line is allowed, and is detected by a time stamp field which is not a number.

Build the undirected line graph in which records e and f are adjacent if the destination of e is the source of f, and e precedes f in time (strictly). The weight of the edge {e, f} is the time difference between e and f, so that each record ranks its neighbors by absolute difference between their time stamps and its own time stamp.

Output is a CSV file without header, whose lines are of the form

(String e, String f, double time difference)

which becomes an input for rbl.jar with Ul as input parameter.

Example:

"java -cp rbl.jar preprocessing.TrafficLineGraphBuilder traffic.csv lineGraph.csv 3600"

"java -jar rbl.jar lineGraph.csv Ul 8"

The optional third argument is a maximum time difference: pairs (e, f) with time(f) - time(e) exceeding it are not linked. Without it, the line graph may have a number of edges quadratic in the number of records.

    • main

      public static void main(String[] args)
      Command-line entry point.

      Expected arguments:

      1. args[0] input CSV file of traffic records
      2. args[1] output CSV file for line-graph edges
      3. (optional) args[2] maximum time difference between linked records
      Parameters:
      args - command-line arguments as described above
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the number of arguments is not 2 or 3

    • readTrafficRecords

      public static List<TrafficRecord> readTrafficRecords(String csvFileName)
      Read records of form (record ID, source, destination, time stamp) from CSV file. A first line whose time stamp is not a number is treated as a header.

      Whitespace around fields is stripped before record creation.

      Parameters:
      csvFileName - name of CSV file
      Returns:
      list of traffic records

    • buildLineGraph

      public void buildLineGraph()
      For each record e, find the records f whose source is the destination of e, and whose time stamp is later than that of e (and within the maximum time difference, if one was given). Records are grouped by source address and sorted by time, so each search is a binary search followed by a scan.

    • writeLineGraphToFile

      public void writeLineGraphToFile(String fileName)
      Write line graph edges as (record ID, record ID, time difference), without header, for use as rbl.jar input with option Ul.
      Parameters:
      fileName - output CSV file
